claim: DORA defines five software delivery performance metrics: throughput (deployment frequency, change lead time) and instability (change fail rate, deployment rework rate, failed deployment recovery time)

span: Metrics as leading and lagging indicators
claim: DORA metrics function as both leading indicators for organizational performance and lagging indicators for software development practices
2025 DORA report found 90% of technology professionals now use AI at work, and over 80% believe it has increased their productivity
AI's primary role in software development is that of an amplifier — it magnifies strengths of high-performing organizations and dysfunctions of struggling ones
Higher AI adoption is associated with increase in both software delivery throughput AND software delivery instability
Time saved by AI in code generation is frequently re-allocated to auditing and verification
Clear AI acceptable-use policies show 451% increase in AI adoption; dedicated learning time leads to 131% increase; transparent communication about job displacement leads to 125% increase
DORA has identified and validated a set of capabilities that drive higher software delivery and organizational performance across technical and process dimensions
Trunk-based development is a core DORA capability that prevents merge-conflict hassles and supports continuous integration
Continuous integration requires small batch sizes, automated builds and tests on every commit, and fast feedback loops
Continuous delivery requires automated deployment pipelines, infrastructure as code, and the ability to deploy on demand
DORA research found a J curve typical of transformation programs — initial efficiency dip before automation and process improvement yield results

When developers are primarily responsible for creating and maintaining automated test suites, it drives improved performance; when other groups own test automation, build pipelines stay broken and developers write hard-to-test code
Teams should strive for a balanced test pyramid: fast unit tests, focused component/contract tests, and lean end-to-end tests
Deployment automation should include progressive rollouts, automated problem detection, and safe rollback capabilities
Teams can make large-scale system changes without permission outside the team, and can deploy independently with negligible downtime when architecture is loosely coupled
Organizational structure and system architecture are linked — loosely coupled teams require loosely coupled architecture
Making code easy to find, reuse, and change, with up-to-date dependencies, drives higher software delivery performance
Clear and communicated AI stance — policies, acceptable-use guidelines, and transparent communication about AI strategy — is a DORA capability that drives AI adoption
100% is the wrong reliability target for most software — error budgets balance innovation velocity with service stability
Postmortems should be blameless, written for all significant incidents, and focused on systemic improvement
Roughly 70% of outages are due to changes in a live system; best practices use automation for progressive rollouts, problem detection, and rollback
SRE can be viewed as a specific implementation of DevOps with idiosyncratic extensions; DevOps is a generalization of core SRE principles
Google caps operational work for SREs at 50% of their time, with remaining time spent on engineering projects
At Google, code review is used to maintain code quality; the best reviewer is the person who can give the most thorough and correct review
Google uses 'changelist' (CL) terminology; LGTM means 'Looks Good to Me' when approving a CL
OWASP DevSecOps pipeline includes: credential scanning, SAST, SCA, IAST, DAST, IaC scanning, infrastructure scanning, and compliance checks
The ideal goal of DevSecOps is to detect security issues as fast as possible, promoting shift-left security culture
NIST SSDF provides a structured framework for secure software development practices across the entire SDLC
GitHub Copilot helps developers code up to 55% faster in enterprise settings (Accenture study)
AI tools adoption in software development continues to grow rapidly, with 97% of surveyed developers having used AI tools
76% of all respondents are using or plan to use AI tools in their development process; 62% are currently using them (up from 44%)
An Internal Developer Platform is built by a platform team to create golden paths and enable developer self-service, consisting of many technologies glued together
The core problem IDPs solve is cognitive load — developers face sprawling tooling landscapes, cloud complexity, and container orchestration challenges
Spotify's yearslong investment in internal development platforms and engineering best practices is driving their AI transition, enabling teams and agents to move faster
Platform engineering has reached mainstream adoption, with communities and certifications emerging for practitioners
The strangler fig pattern allows iterative replacement of monolithic architecture with componentized architecture
Backward-compatible versioned APIs with no more than two concurrent supported versions, with six-month transition periods before retirement
OpenTelemetry has become the de facto standard for observability instrumentation in cloud-native environments
SREs should receive a maximum of two events per 8-12 hour on-call shift; more indicates systemic problems, less indicates waste
